newsitem.title: ZAIRE: Residents say looting aid at Zaire rebel urging.
newsitem.headline: Residents say looting aid at Zaire rebel urging.

text.p: Zairean residents armed with knives and machetes said they were looting aid on Monday at the urging of rebels and blamed Rwandan Hutus for the killing of six villagers.
Eastern Provincial Governor Yagi Sitolo told Reuters up to eight Zaireans were killed by Rwandan Hutu refugees who attacked their village 25 km (15 miles) south of Kisangani earlier on Monday.
"There is tension across the (Zaire) river and this morning we heard the population is angry because the refugees killed six or eight Zairean people," Sitolo told Reuters in Kisangani.
"That is why we sent a group to see what has happened there."
In Geneva, U.N. refugee agency chief Sadako Ogata said a rebel military operation near Kasese camp 25 km (15 miles) south of Kisangani raised the prospect of a new Rwandan refugee exodus.
Residents of Lula, seven km (four miles) south of the city, said Rwandan refugees attacked a village near Kasese camp, with 32,000 refugees, before dawn and killed at least six people.

Some of the angry residents armed with knives and pangas told Reuters they spent the morning and part of the night looting aid vehicles at the urging of the Tutsi-dominated rebels, who seized the northeastern capital of Kisangani on March 15.

"The liberators (rebels) sent us here to pillage things going to the refugees. When we got back to the roadblock they (the rebels) took the things from us," said one young man who declined to be named.
"We are angry because the refugees have killed our people so we are here to loot any vehicle that goes past," another said.
Aid workers had said they feared residents who looted aid warehouses and stopped aid workers from reaching Rwandan refugee camps south of Kisangani were doing so with rebel encouragement.
The rebels denied any involvement in the unrest. Villagers attacked a train loaded with 120 tonnes of food near Lula early on Monday and looted a World Food Programme further south.
Rebels stopped journalists from passing their checkpoint but foreign journalists earlier saw the bodies of six Zairean villagers whom residents said were killed by Rwandan Hutu militiamen.
